{{Nihongo|'''Heijō Shrine'''|平壌神社|Heijō jinja|lead=yes|{{Korean|hangul=평양신사}}}} was a [[Shinto]] shrine in {{ill|Pyongyang|en|Pyongyang|qid=Q18808|lt=Pyongyang}}, Korea during the {{ill|Korea under Japanese rule|en|Korea under Japanese rule|qid=Q503585|lt=Japanese colonial period}}. It was established in 1913<ref>{{Cite web |title=平壌神社 {{!}} 　海外神社（跡地）に関するデータベース　神奈川大学非文字資料研究センター |url=http://www.himoji.jp/database/db04/permalink.php?id=2663 |access-date=2023-10-09 |website=www.himoji.jp}}</ref> and destroyed in 1945.<ref name=":0" />

Its name derived from the Japanese name for Pyongyang during its occupation of Korea. The shrine's main annual festival was held on October 2. It was formerly a national shrine of the third Rank (国幣小社, ''[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]'') in the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

The shrine was destroyed on August 16, 1945: just after {{ill|Surrender of Japan|en|Surrender of Japan|qid=Q6540361|lt=Japan first announced its surrender}} in World War II. That day, local Koreans set fire to the shrine and destroyed it. Hundreds of similar cases arose throughout the peninsula in the following week.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=神社참배 거부 18개교 日帝, 가차 없이 폐교｜주간동아 |url=https://weekly.donga.com/society/3/05/11/77546/1 |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=주간동아 |language=ko}}</ref>

In modern times, the site is a park, with a statue of {{ill|Kim Il Sung|en|Kim Il Sung|qid=Q41117|lt=Kim Il Sung}} built at the site of the shrine's building.

'''Heijō Shrine''' was a {{jalink|神社|Q845945|shrine}} located in Heijō-fu, {{jalink|平安南道 (日本統治時代)|Q11060859|Heian-nan Province}}, {{jalink|日本統治時代の朝鮮|Q503585|Korea under Japanese rule}} (now {{jalink|朝鮮民主主義人民共和国|Q423|North Korea}} {{jalink|平壌直轄市|Pyongyang}}). Its former {{jalink|社格|Q10444029|shrine rank}} was {{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|Kokuhei Shōsha}}<ref name=国体神祇辞典/>.

The {{jalink|祭神|Q11591100|enshrined deities}} were {{jalink|天照大神|Q455602|Amaterasu Ōmikami}} and {{jalink|国魂|Q9692242|Kunitama Ōkami}}<ref name=国体神祇辞典>{{オープンアクセス}}[{{NDLDC|1909346/829}} 『国体神祇辞典』小倉鏗爾著 (錦正堂, 1940)  - 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション] 1505頁（2018年1月30日閲覧）</ref>.

== History ==
The enshrinement ceremony was held on {{jalink|1月1日|Q2150|January 1}}, {{jalink|1913年|Q2080|1913}} ({{jalink|大正|Q329174|Taishō}} 2), and it became an official shrine on {{jalink|5月4日|Q2549|May 4}}, {{jalink|1916年|Q2087|1916}} (Taishō 5). A new {{jalink|神社建築|Q3080012|shrine building}} was completed in September {{jalink|1936年|Q18649|1936}} ({{jalink|昭和|Q327567|Shōwa}} 11)<ref name=国体神祇辞典/>, and on {{jalink|5月15日|Q2562|May 15}}, {{jalink|1937年|Q18647|1937}} (Shōwa 12), it was elevated to the rank of Kokuhei Shōsha together with {{jalink|大邱神社|Q11439410|Taegu Shrine}} in {{jalink|大邱広域市|Q20927|Taegu-fu}}, {{jalink|慶尚北道 (日本統治時代)|Q625101|Keishō-hokudō}}<ref name=国体神祇辞典/>. On the night of {{jalink|8月15日|Q2774|August 15}}, {{jalink|1945年|Q5240|1945}} (Shōwa 20), when {{jalink|日本の降伏|Q6540361|Japan's surrender}} in {{jalink|第二次世界大戦|Q362|World War II}} was announced to the nation through the {{jalink|玉音放送|Q709465|Imperial Rescript}}, Heijō Shrine was destroyed by arson<ref>{{Cite book|和書|author=森田芳夫|title=朝鮮終戦の記録 : 米ソ両軍の進駐と日本人の引揚|publisher=巌南堂書店|date=1964-08-15|pages=182|id={{NDLJP|3014647/107}}}}</ref>. It was subsequently abolished without being rebuilt.

The shrine site was located at the southern end of a small {{jalink|丘|Q54050|hill}} called {{jalink|牡丹峰|Q717264|Moranbong}}, a scenic spot in Pyongyang. In 1946, the {{jalink|牡丹峰劇場|Moranbong Theater}} was constructed on the former site of Heijō Shrine<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|title=うまれかわる朝鮮――｢北朝鮮紀行｣より / 徐光霽|journal=新しい世界|issue=24|publisher=日本共産党出版局事業部|date=1949-07-01|pages=35|id={{NDLJP|3542933/19}}}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=城戸又一|title=素顔の社会主義国 : 十人のジャーナリストは報告する|publisher=東洋書館|date=1956-12-15|pages=140|id={{NDLJP|2975357/74}}}}</ref>.
